Space exploration has always been driven by the relentless pursuit of human curiosity, propelled by groundbreaking innovations in technology. Rockets, as the bearers of astronauts and payloads to the orbit, have been central to this endeavor, enabling us to venture beyond the boundaries of Earth's gravity and explore the vast expanse of the universe. The challenge of overcoming gravity is a fundamental aspect of space travel, as rockets must generate enough thrust to break free from the gravitational pull of our home planet and achieve the necessary velocity to enter and remain in orbit. This critical phase of space exploration has revolutionized our understanding of the cosmos, paving the way for future missions to other planets and celestial bodies, all fueled by the relentless pursuit of scientific discovery and human achievement.
